finding: The client/driver axis is not comparable across resources: what each resource calls a role is a different measurement
evidence: DrLLPS Scaffold->driver and Client->client; PhaSepDB client/driver; LLPSDB and PhasePro contribute ONLY driver (they are in-vitro LLPS databases with no client concept); CDCODE contributes no role at all (13,758 assertions, 38% of the dataset)
biological_impact: A 'driver' from PhasePro means 'this purified protein phase-separates in vitro'; a 'driver' from PhaSepDB means 'reported as essential for condensate formation in cells'; a DrLLPS 'Scaffold' means 'annotated as scaffold by DrLLPS curators'. Pooling them into one column makes the driver class a mixture of three different claims
recommended_action: Keep unified_role but add a mandatory evidence_type column (in_vitro_llps | cellular_requirement | curator_assignment) so the three claims can be filtered apart

finding: 42.2% of distinct assertions carry no role, and the missingness is entirely resource-determined
evidence: 15,147 of 35,925 assertions have unified_role NULL: all 13,758 CDCODE assertions plus the 1,389 DrLLPS Regulator rows
biological_impact: Any per-MLO driver/client ratio is really a statement about which resources annotate that MLO. An MLO covered only by CDCODE has no role information at all, not a 'balanced' composition
recommended_action: Report role coverage per MLO alongside any role-based statistic; never compute driver fraction over rows that include roleless resources

finding: Role is assigned at protein level and propagated to every MLO the protein belongs to, not measured per compartment
evidence: In DrLLPS, all 1,055 proteins annotated in more than one MLO carry an identical role in every one of them (0 exceptions); scaffold proteins average 2.4 MLOs each, up to 8. In PhaSepDB only 26.2% of multi-MLO proteins vary their role
biological_impact: The model asserts that being a driver is a property of the protein, not of the protein-compartment pair. This is biologically wrong: FUS drives stress granules but is a client of the nucleolus. The database cannot currently express that
recommended_action: Document that role is protein-scoped in the upstream sources; do not present it as a per-MLO property in the served schema, or mark DrLLPS-derived roles as propagated

finding: driver_share per MLO is determined by dataset availability, not by condensate biology
evidence: heterochromatin, inclusion_body and transcriptional_condensate are 100% driver (n=53-109) purely because no resource contributes a bulk client proteome for them; nucleolus is 2.1% driver because DrLLPS and PhaSepDB contribute 5,463 client assertions
biological_impact: Reading these fractions as 'the nucleolus is mostly clients while heterochromatin is all drivers' inverts cause and effect: the ratio measures whether someone did a proteomic survey of that compartment
recommended_action: Do not expose driver_share as a biological metric without the client-source flag; add has_bulk_proteome per MLO

finding: Cross-resource role agreement is high between the two large resources but breaks down against in-vitro sources
evidence: PhaSepDB vs DrLLPS: 90.9% agreement over 1,608 shared assertions (51 driver/client, 96 client/driver disagreements). PhaSepDB vs PhasePro: 58.6% over 70 shared, with 29 client-vs-driver reversals; DrLLPS vs LLPSDB: 100% over 98
biological_impact: The 41% disagreement with PhasePro is the predicted consequence of ROL-01: proteins that phase-separate in vitro are routinely clients in cells. It is not curation noise, it is the two claim types disagreeing
recommended_action: Use the disagreement set as a labelled example set when defining evidence_type; publish it as a QC table

finding: Regulator exclusion is applied at row level, silently removing proteins entirely
evidence: 1,389 DrLLPS Regulator assertions are marked dataset_active=0; 502 proteins have no other annotation and disappear from the served dataset
biological_impact: Regulators (kinases, chaperones, RNA helicases that tune condensate assembly) are a legitimate and biologically informative class; removing them biases the dataset toward structural components and removes the enzymes that control assembly
recommended_action: Serve Regulator as a third role value with a clear definition instead of excluding it, or expose the excluded rows behind a flag

finding: 18% of driver assertions come from resources that only ever say driver
evidence: 558 of 3,111 driver assertions originate in LLPSDB (380) and PhasePro (178), neither of which has a client category
biological_impact: These resources cannot contribute a negative; their presence inflates the driver class without evidence that the protein is not a client
recommended_action: Weight or flag single-valued sources when computing driver enrichment
